source.title: ParaScopes: What do Language Models Activations Encode About Future Text?
source.authors: Nicky Pochinkov; Yu.G. Volkova; Anna Vasileva; Sai V. R. Chereddy

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether future paragraph content is decodable from activations using residual-stream decoders and similarity/judge measures, rather than the original future-token probes or rhyme intervention.
record.gate_note: The study reports paragraph- and outline-level decoding results, layer-wise and token-wise analyses, and metrics against baselines. It does not test rhyming verse or intervene on candidate rhyme words. Cheat-token and regeneration figures are comparison baselines, not tests of the activation-based claim itself.
record.test_reason: The study decodes upcoming-paragraph and outline content from a single position's residual stream in Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct and Gemma-2-9B, scored against random and cheat-K baselines. This is a different method aimed at V2's question. Its token-wise and outline results also bear on V6's 'shallow, only-immediate' planning.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Residual streams at paragraph boundaries hold partially decodable information about the next paragraph, comparable to a 5-10-token lookahead, and concentrated in middle layers. Outline-level signal is weak. The token-wise myopia ('just-in-time' plan creation at \n\n) is shown in Gemma-2-9B, while the main decoding results are in Llama-3.2-3B. Causal relevance to model performance is left open.
record.recipe_differences: Uses residual-stream replacement for continuation and a trained map to SONAR embeddings, evaluated on paragraph and outline content; does not use the original future-token probing or rhyme-word intervention method.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by decoding method and metric: TAE better preserves subject match, while Continuation sometimes scores better on fine-grained details. The strongest layer effects are reported at layers 25-35, and future-topic similarity changes across pre-transition, transition, and post-transition positions.
record.problems: The authors say the study is primarily limited to one model for the main paragraph experiments, short structured paragraphs, and methods that do not establish strict causal contribution to model performance. They note possible embedding-model confounds and that plans may be distributed across tokens. Reported results also differ between the main-section cosine metric and Appendix C.1 metrics.

untested.parts: No rhyming verse, no rhyme-word representations, no interventions on candidate endings.
Exact token-level prediction at specific future positions is not measured; only semantic, paragraph-level similarity and judged content match.
No test separating pre-caching from breadcrumbs, or of whether features are computed because they help later positions.
Open-weight models are used, but there is no rhyme-planning test with attribution graphs or probes.
No multi-step reasoning, chess or Sokoban tasks.
No causal test in the original generation context of whether the decoded plans steer the text actually written.

missing.what: LLM-judge entity-preservation and coherence comparisons (TAE stronger on subjects/entities, Continuation more coherent), reported only qualitatively
Cosine values for cheat-1 and cheat-10 baselines and the saturation of cheat-K at ~20 tokens, needed to interpret the 'equivalent to 5+ tokens' claim

record.verdict_notes: Main experiments use one model, Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct; the token-wise analysis uses Gemma-2-9B. Layer-scrubbing rows are likely Gemma-2-9B, given the 42 layers. Appendix F and G statistics lack baselines. The outline target model is called 'Llama 3.2 70B' (likely Llama 3.3 70B). Whether the paragraph-level results support or challenge V6 depends on whether 'a few tokens ahead' is read as horizon or as information content. The study gives paragraph-horizon topic information equivalent to about 5 tokens of content.

versions.untested_parts: Rhyme-word representations and interventions that change the intermediate line.
Exact token prediction several positions ahead is not directly measured; the main outcomes concern semantic similarity and judged content match at paragraph or outline scale.
The study does not distinguish pre-caching from breadcrumbs or test whether decoded features are computed specifically because they help later positions.
No rhyme-planning test in smaller open-weight models using attribution graphs or probing tools.
No multi-step reasoning, chess, or Sokoban look-ahead test.
The study does not establish that the detected signals are merely local next-token features or heuristics, and it does not causally test whether they steer intermediate text.

relationships.condition: Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, transition-token residual, paragraph-level topic content; Gemma-2-9B at the transition token
relationships.reason: Both ParaScopes beat the random baseline on cosine similarity (0.43/0.55 vs 0.20), BLEURT and judged subject match (76%/43% vs 4%). Gemma reaches 0.48 at the transition (r1-r4, r24, r25, r27, r28, r16, r19).
relationships.display_finding: The two ParaScopes achieved cosine similarities of 0.43/0.55 versus 0.20 and subject matches of 76%/43% versus 4%, also outperforming the baseline on BLEURT; Gemma reached 0.48 cosine similarity at the transition.

source_check.condition: Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, transition-token residual, paragraph-level topic content; Gemma-2-9B at the transition token
source_check.reason: The boundary residual supports above-baseline recovery of upcoming paragraph content in the stated semantic-content condition; exact-token accuracy is not established.

relationships.condition: Fine-grained details, outline scale, and positions before the paragraph boundary
relationships.reason: Moderate-detail recovery is only 3-15%, against 79% for regeneration. Outline detail match is 24%. In Gemma the future topic is near-absent before the transition (0.12) (r7, r8, r11, r9, r10, r15, r18).
relationships.display_finding: Moderate-detail recovery was 3–15% versus 79% for regeneration, outline detail match was 24%, and Gemma's pre-transition topic recovery score was 0.12.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Fine-grained details, outline scale, and positions before the paragraph boundary
source_check.reason: Detail recovery is weak, outline results are limited, and Gemma's future-topic signal depends strongly on the position read.

relationships.condition: Token-wise dynamics in Gemma-2-9B, outline decoding, and cheat-K equivalence in Llama-3.2-3B
relationships.reason: Several results point to shallow planning. Next-paragraph topic appears only at \n\n (0.12 before, 0.48 at). Outline details are weak (24%). Decoded information is comparable to about 5 revealed tokens. Authors call this 'relatively myopic' (r15, r18, r19, r9-r11, r1, r2).
relationships.display_finding: Next-paragraph topic scores rose from 0.12 before the double newline to 0.48 at it, outline-detail decoding reached 24%, and decoded information resembled about 5 revealed tokens.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Token-wise dynamics in Gemma-2-9B, outline decoding, and cheat-K equivalence in Llama-3.2-3B
source_check.reason: Cheat-5-equivalent decoding, weak outline details, and the abrupt boundary appearance of the next topic support shallow or just-in-time planning in these settings.

relationships.condition: Paragraph-level topic decoding at the boundary and middle-layer patching
relationships.reason: At the boundary the residual carries the topic of a whole ~50-token paragraph, not just next-token features. Swapping middle-layer activations (25-35) shifts the continued topic (delta 0.15-0.25), so the signal is more than local heuristics within the probe context (r3, r13, r16, r19).
relationships.display_finding: Boundary activations encoded the topic of an approximately 50-token paragraph, and swapping activations in layers 25–35 shifted probe continuations’ topics by 0.15–0.25.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Paragraph-level topic decoding at the boundary and middle-layer patching
source_check.reason: Topic decoding and steering a blank-context probe do not establish a horizon beyond a few cue tokens or rule out local features and heuristics. Whether the decoded representation steers original-context generation is untested.

tranche.reason: Residual-stream continuation and learned text-embedding decoders investigate future-content information using a different method and measure.

source_check.notes: Section 6.1 leaves its 42-layer model unnamed; attribution to Gemma is an inference. Section 5's TAE minimal-detail comparison (52%) conflicts with Section 4 (TAE 57%, Continuation 52%).

statements.correction: Boundary TAE subject match ≥2: 76%, random 4%. Section 6.1: unspecified 42-layer model; layers 25–35 produce cosine deltas 0.15–0.25 in Continuation ParaScope. Gemma transition similarity: 0.48 ±0.15. Main decoding performance: comparable to cheat-5.
statements.problem: The reported decoding and patching numbers are correct, but they do not establish content beyond the first cue tokens: performance is comparable to cheat-5, and original-context causal relevance remains untested.
